newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah guerrillas attack Israeli-backed militia.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah guerrillas attack Israeli-backed militia.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas attacked a fortified outpost of Israel's militia allies in south Lebanon on Sunday causing damage but no casualties, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
The guerrillas fired mortar bombs at a post of the Israeli-allied South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia at Jamoos in the western flank of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, SLA sources said.
They said an ammunition depot and a fuel tank received direct hits, causing fires to break out in them.

In Beirut, the Islamic Resistance, the military wing of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah group, claimed responsibility for the attack saying it caused casualties. Hizbollah said a tank was destroyed and an ammunition depot was hit.

Hizbollah (Party of God), which leads the guerrilla war on Israeli and SLA forces in south Lebanon, also said in its statement that its fighters clashed with Israeli soldiers near the village of Haddatha and attacked another force near Tiri.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the two assaults in the zone's western sector.
On Saturday, Israeli jets attacked Hizbollah targets in south Lebanon highlands hours after an SLA patrol was ambushed.

Some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong SLA hold the zone stretching along the Lebanese side of border from Mount Hermon in the east to the Mediterranean westwards since 1985 to ward off cross-frontier guerrilla raids on northern Israel.
